## Next version: RS-A-foldkeys and RS-A-trailingdot (2026-11-10, branch `claude/rs-a-foldkeys` off f97553a, merged in PR #39 as b53b065)

Both were deferred from PR #38's reviews and flagged as serious: they are about access (a folder or file the check never looks at), on Windows. The user pulled them in on 2026-11-10.

- RS-A-foldkeys, the fault, CONFIRMED here on f97553a (Windows, `repro-fold.js` in the session's scratchpad; each case below is also in the test). Four sets of "already seen" (five keyed places, since one set is keyed at two) were keyed by `toLowerCase()` on Windows, and JavaScript lower-cases `k` and the Kelvin sign (U+212A) alike while NTFS and ReFS keep them as two names. With the look-alike named first, the second was skipped and the answer was `''`:
  - `farConfig`'s set of config files read: `.git/config` including `k.cfg`, then `<U+212A>.cfg` whose `core.attributesFile` names a share. Alone: `network-config`.
  - `linkedEntries`' set of folders walked: `.git/refs/heads/k` next to `.git/refs/heads/<U+212A>` holding a junction loop. Alone: `linked-gitdir`.
  - `moduleGitdirs`' set, twice: `.git/modules/k` next to a gitdir `.git/modules/<U+212A>` whose config names a share (`farModules`), and the same for the `objects` folder of two such gitdirs.
  - `farGitConfig`'s set of folders searched for a `.git`: the session in `w/k/link`, a junction to `w/<U+212A>/sub`, where `w/k` is a repo whose config names a share. From a plain folder there: `network-config`.
  - The review named the second and guessed at the third and fourth; the first and the last are new, found by searching for the pattern.
- The fix: each set is keyed by the exact text. A config file named again in another case is read again, within the 50 files. A folder a link leads to is told by the system's own path for it (`onDisk`, rounds 1 to 3 below), so the walks' sets know it under one text.
- RS-A-trailingdot, the fault, CONFIRMED here on f97553a: Windows programs drop dots and spaces from a name's end, and Node opens the name as written. `cmd /c dir k.` lists `k`; `k./a` reaches `k/a`. With `lfs.storage = <path>/k.`, git-lfs 3.8.1 reports `LfsStorageDir=.../k.` and `git add` of a tracked file writes the object into `k/objects/...` (run here). `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run with the folder `k.` answers `.../k` (run here). The check answered `''` for `lfs.storage = k.`, `k..`, `k./a` (the folder `k` holding a junction loop) and for a session folder given as `k.` (the repo `k` naming a share in its config).
  - Not a fault: a `.git` file with `gitdir: ../real.`. git itself answers "gitfile does not point to a valid repository" (run here).
- The fix: `dotEnd(p)`, Windows only: a path with a name that ends in a dot or a space, `.` and `..` apart. It is refused in `oddRelative` (a value, an include, an alternates line, a pointer, a link's target: `odd-config-path` or the caller's reason), in `farGitConfig` for the session folder and `farNested` for a nested repo's (`odd-path`), and in `localPath` itself (never a local path, whoever asks). Since round 1 (below) one caller is left out: values under `alias` and `pretty` (`WORDS_KEY`), where `farPathValue` asks `driveRelative` in place of `oddRelative` and passes `words` to `localPath`. Quoted values (`storage = "k "`) are decoded before the check and refused too (run here through a real config file).
- The test: "git pointers: two names JavaScript lower-cases alike are two names, and a name Windows opens under another is refused (next version)". It fails on f97553a's `gitbin.js` in both copies. 16 single changes of the fix each fail it: 15 on Windows, and the Windows-only switch of `dotEnd` in WSL (where `k.` must stay a name like any other). The list is `muts-fold.json` in the scratchpad, not kept in the repo. One junction is made, on Windows only, with `busyRetry`.
- What a user can meet: on Windows, a config value, include, pointer or session folder with a name that ends in a dot or a space is now refused. For a file's or folder's name that was INFERRED never in a real repo (Windows programs can't make or open such a name); round 1 showed it wrong for values that are not paths, and aliases and log formats are now left out (below). Still refused: a path setting, or a key of one's own that ends like one, whose value has a word ending in a dot or a space at its end or before a slash. A file system that folds `k` and the Kelvin sign (macOS's) has one folder for the two, which the checks then read once for each text.

## Next version: RS-A-storagewalk (2026-11-10, branch `claude/rs-a-storagewalk` off afe9bf9, merged in PR #38 as f97553a)

The user pulled it in on 2026-11-10 ("Yes, fix storagewalk"), after PR #37 merged.

- The fault, CONFIRMED here on afe9bf9 (Windows): `lfs.storage` in 200 spellings of one folder with 10,100 entries through `farLfsEntries` is accepted in 2.7 s, with 200 `statSync` and 200 `readdirSync` calls. 52,000 spellings of an empty folder (16 parts of `./` or `.//` each) are refused after 4.9 s and 45,636 calls of each. `farPathValue` kept its set of walked folders for one value only, and the work limit doesn't count a store's walk.
- The fix (`gitbin.js`, both copies): the folders `lfs.storage` values led to are kept for one check (`STORES`, set by `limitedWalk` like the lookup cache), by the exact path `localPath` found (lower-cased on Windows in 3dbc23c, which round 1 showed wrong; see below). A folder or file already seen under the same path text costs no disk call. Two limits bound what that leaves: more than 64 different folders (`MAX_LFS_STORES`), and no further folder once those before it held 20,000 looked-at entries between them (`MAX_STORE_ENTRIES`; `linkedEntries` reports the count through `tally`). Past either the answer is `many-config-paths`.
- Why two limits: the first version had only the 64. Folders of files are cheap (64 of 12,000 files: 1.3 s), but 64 stores laid out as git-lfs does it (`objects/ab/cd`, 10,100 folders each) were accepted in 45 s, CONFIRMED here before the commit. One such store takes 0.65 to 0.8 s on Windows: that is older behavior (the store budget of 10,000 entries), not changed here.

A `core.worktree` counts once for each folder its file is in (it is taken from there), and `lfs.storage` is a kind of its own (its folder is walked). More than 200 different values (`MAX_PATH_VALUES`), or more than 8 different `core.worktree` values (`MAX_WORKTREE_VALUES`), in 578532e (the review batch below changed both numbers), keep git out with a new reason, `many-config-paths`, before anything is walked. `farLfsEntries` now walks its path values after the whole file is read, so a file with a bad path value before an include answers `lfs-config` where it answered the path's reason; both keep git out.

Reach, INFERRED from the order of events, not run: it needs a compaction's entry written between one hook's transcript read and its save, with a second hook starting in that gap. The fix would be a cycle identity in the state, a bigger change to code that has had five rounds of race reviews.

After the fix an 8 MB value and the 500,000-part value are each refused in about 10 to 25 ms.

The commit-list control (`sinceInTime`, `handoff-checks.test.js`), as of d4ab59c: the tests' sandbox sets `JBMEM_SHOW_SINCE=1`, and the launcher (`sinceHandoff`, both copies) then writes `trailmark since: late elapsed=<ms> left=<ms> budget=<ms> git=<ms>` to stderr when the commit list runs out of time. It only reports, no budget changes. Each session start that says git ran out of time must show the launcher's rule held (the time left is 5000 - elapsed - 1500 within 50 ms, with elapsed measured apart; git's budget is min(1,200, left), or 0 under 400 ms left) and that time really ran out: under 400 ms left before git ran, or git spent its budget less 300 ms (the runner refuses a call with under 250 ms left, so a real timeout spends at least budget - 250). After three in a row, the test skips only if the same lookup with 30 s answers. History: round 1 replaced a floor on the lookup alone (900 ms), which failed a slowdown before git (Opus #2), with whole-run floors; those held at 8 and 16 busy loops only because the first of three starts came in under 1,200 ms (up to 1,184 ms), and the duplicate session batch-f-2 saw a whole-run floor let a forced 0 ms budget skip at 37 to 68% CPU (CONFIRMED by batch-f-2, not re-run), so bfa24ad reads the launcher's report instead, and d4ab59c checks the rule behind `left` and `budget` (review round 3: a left of `5000 - elapsed - 4800` skipped all 14 at rest). Proof on d4ab59c's code with forced faults (scratch, `bf-force2.py` and `bf-force3.py`): at rest, nothing forced 14 pass; the left formula broken (`- 4800`), 14 fail; git's cap at 450 ms, 13 fail and 1 passes (git fit in 450 that time); budget 0, 14 fail (and 14 under 16 busy loops); 3.2 s before `sinceHandoff`, 14 skip; every git call out of time, 14 fail; git log failing, 8 fail; git log faked out of time, 12 fail; 48 busy loops, nothing forced, 12 skip and 2 pass. Earlier, on bfa24ad's code (scratch, `bf-force2.py` and `bf-force-slow.py`), the 14 commit-list tests in both copies: at rest, nothing forced 14 pass; the launcher's budget forced to 0 ms, 14 fail; a 3.2 s busy-wait before `sinceHandoff`, 14 skip (left 186 ms or less); every git call of `commitsSince` out of time, 14 fail; git log failing (not time), 8 fail; git log faked as out of time on its first call, 12 fail (it reports git 444 to 520 ms of 1,200: not a real timeout) and 2 pass. Under busy loops: 16, nothing forced 14 pass and budget 0 fails 14; 32, nothing forced 14 pass and budget 0 fails 14; 48, nothing forced 12 skip (git spent 954 to 1,155 ms of 1,200) and 2 pass. None of the nothing-forced runs failed (CONFIRMED, 2026-11-07).

("...: git could not list them.", or "... to fit the budget." as before).

## Load-proof tests (2026-11-07, branch `claude/load-proof-tests` off 5566010)

PR #14 (https://github.com/cptjamestiberiouskirk-pixel/trailmark/pull/14), opened 2026-11-07 after review round 3 and a merge of main (208d5fb, 5579e63, then 0a8a666 for a conflict here). It waits for its 9 jobs and the user's word to merge.

The goal: no test fails because shipped code ran out of a wall-clock budget it is designed to run out of. Fixed in the tests only: no shipped file and no environment setting changed (so no security row). Each test that needs a budget's in-time path now repeats the call while its result shows that budget's out-of-time sign, as the sweep tests' `settle()` does. Where the sign names time for certain, the test skips with the reason after the repeats. Where it doesn't (the commit list), it fails after three tries, so a fault that always gives the sign still fails. Any other reason for an early stop fails at once.

Budgets in `plugins/trailmark/scripts` and what covers them:

| Budget | Where | Tests that need it in time | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| copy check 300 ms | `health.js:170` (`otherCopies`); session start `trailmark.js:365`, `--copies` `:711` | 13 handoff-checks copy and rename tests and `copiesOf`'s users, 6 in `copies.test.js` (per copy) | `copiesInTime` (handoff-checks: repeat for 30 s, then skip), `walkInTime`, `startInTime`, `listInTime` (`copies.test.js`: five tries, then the result as it is) |
| commit list, at most 1.2 s | `trailmark.js:406` (`sinceHandoff`), `gitfacts.js:703` (`commitsSince`) | 7 handoff-checks tests | `sinceInTime`: three tries, then the result as it is |
| git facts and commit facts, 5 s less what the launcher used | `trailmark.js:341`, `:350` | basics "launcher: hooks run sandboxed ...", commits "0.3.3 hardening: the PreCompact status ...", sweep "0.3.4 commits: another session's commit ...", sessions "hooks: a busy lock costs the reminder ..." (since review round 2) | `lateAgain` (three tries, then skip) and `inTimeTest` (skip; that step can't be repeated); the busy-lock test repeats its commit hook in a loop of its own (three tries, then skip) |
| the launcher's hook limit, 4.5 s for commit-start, 9 s for the others | `trailmark.js:219` | sessions "hooks: a busy lock costs the reminder ...", security "0.5.1 commit hook: a background commit command ..." | `hookInTime` (three tries, then skip), `hookTest`; each try a new tool-call ID |
| a busy lock's wait, 2 s | `store.js:679` (`updateState`) | the busy-lock test's old 6 s bound on the whole hook | timed in the test's own process: `updateState` against the held lock must give up within 4 s |
| sweep 3 s | `trailmark.js:471`, `:537`, `:655`; `gitfacts.js:641` | the sweep tests | unchanged: they already skip (`sweepTest`) |
| commit-start's command parse, 300 ms (1.5 s by default) | `hook-commit-start.js:42`, `commands.js:2149` | none seen failing; a test command parses in well under 1 ms | unchanged |
| a git call's own 3 s; the module walk's `left() < 800` | `paths.js:67`, `:79`; `gitbin.js:355`, `:760`, `:918` | none seen failing | unchanged |
| Windows rename retry 2 s | `store.js:202` | the junction tests (EPERM/EBUSY, B8) | unchanged |

A first run, while the lock subagent's busy loops ran, failed 6 of 14 with the section missing in all three tries: load as its cause is INFERRED from the timing |

So a fault that makes a budget always run out still fails tests for every budget covered: the copy check's direct walks and, since review round 1, `--copies` (F3), the commit-list tests, the rest of `commits.test.js` and `basics.test.js`, and the hook tests in `sessions.test.js` and `security.test.js`. The busy-lock and hook-limit rows are CONFIRMED by the subagent that made those fixes (report in the review-strategy session's notes folder, `load-proof/lockhook-report.md`), the git-facts rows by the one that made those (`load-proof/gitfacts-report.md`), not re-run here; the whole-file rows for git facts and the hook limit, and every copy-check and commit-list row, are CONFIRMED here. No timing is compared between old and new: the runs weren't alternated.

What is still load-sensitive, and why:

- The commit list fails after three tries in a row (every call late: 14 of 14 fail, by design). The text doesn't say git ran out, so a skip there could hide a fault. The product fix stays deferred ("Session start's commit list under load").
- 0.3.4's last step: the side pass for another session's folders (`gitfacts.js:547`, about 1 s) can run out without writing any marker, so the test still fails there with no sign to key on (HYPOTHESIZED cause of the 13:02 failure, as before).
- The busy-lock test no longer catches a hook that waits on the lock twice (INFERRED from the code: two 2 s waits stay inside the 9 s limit, so nothing stops the hook). A hook with a longer wait of its own did pass it on 91415bb, by skipping (CONFIRMED, review round 1 F1, below); since round 1 that fails when the run with the lock free leaves room for the wait. Comparing the hook against itself without the lock can't fill the rest under load: the difference swung from -0.7 to +6 s (CONFIRMED by the subagent's measurement).
- In the commit-start test, the milestone hook after it and the first session start can hit their 9 s limit too; they aren't repeated, since repeating them isn't proven safe (INFERRED).
- A session start cut short while `--show-names` finished, with no time reason from `--show-names` in ten tries, fails the copy tests (review round 2, C). In a simulation with session start late on 99% of calls and `--show-names` on 50%, that is 0.09% of calls; at equal rates (90% or 99%) none in 20,000. The real rates are HYPOTHESIZED. It stays so a fault of session start's own still fails.
- The busy-lock test's commit hook, stopped three times with the lock busy, fails if the same hook with the lock removed then takes under 6 s. With the commit hook as its own control, a steady load can't fail it (INFERRED from round 2's timings: 11 to 12.5 s free at 24 busy loops). A changing load can: it needs three stops of 9 s or more, then a free run under 6 s, so the free run more than 3 s faster beyond the lock's wait, and the hook against itself swung by up to +6 s (line above). So a false failure is HYPOTHESIZED possible, never seen; the three-stop chain was never reached in a loaded run.
- "copies: the command the note gives ..." keeps its round 3 to 5 form (it accepts a check that ran out, with diagnostics) rather than repeating, so it still checks less under load.
- `list()` in `health.js` (lines 133 and 150) reports any error opening or reading a folder, other than ENOENT, as "<folder> has too many folders". CONFIRMED by a probe (`probe-list.js`, scratch): EBUSY and EPERM, at open and mid-read, both give "the plugin cache has too many folders". Whether Windows gives such a transient error there is HYPOTHESIZED, never seen. The tests don't repeat on it: it isn't the time reason, so a test fails with that wording, which now points at this item. Decided: a read error should be a reason of its own ("could not be read"), but that changes shipped wording (what `--copies --show-names` prints; no shipped doc names the reason, CONFIRMED by grep), so it goes to the next version with the docs and Opus rows; see "Deferred to the next version".

### Review round 1 (`git diff 5566010..91415bb`, 2026-11-07)

Opus, regression and design (the diff touches tests and `dev/` only, so no security or docs row). Report in the review-strategy session's notes folder, `load-proof/review1.md`. Four findings, each reproduced here before the fix; fixed in one push:

- F1 (CONFIRMED, reproduced: with `updateState`'s wait at 20 s in `hook-milestone.js`, the busy-lock test skipped 2 of 2 in 33 s on 91415bb). A lock that hangs the hook read as a slow machine. Fix: after three stops with the lock busy, `hookInTime` runs the subagent hook once with the lock free; if that run takes under 6 s (9 s limit, less the 2 s wait, less 1 s), the test fails, else it skips as before. The margin keeps a slow machine from failing it: a free run near the limit says nothing. (Wrong for the commit hook on d6a01ac: its free run was the subagent hook, which took 30 to 40% of the commit hook's free time in round 2's timings; round 2, A.) Proof: the new test fails in both copies (2 of 2, "took 409 ms with it free" and 398 ms) with the 20 s wait; 2/2 pass as shipped.
- F2 (CONFIRMED, reproduced: `probe-helpers.js` drove the old `copiesInTime` 1,708,788 times in 0.3 s, then it threw the skip). A session start cut short for a reason of its own ("the check failed": its call threw) while `--show-names` finished was repeated until the 30 s ran out, then skipped. Session start's note gives no reason, so the helper now tries that case five times and returns the result, and the test fails on it. (Five tries also failed on time alone, since both walks have the same budget; round 2, C.) The comment that said every reason stops every check the same way is corrected. Proof: the same probe gives the result after 5 tries; its other five cases give what they gave before.
- F3 (CONFIRMED by the reviewer, not re-run on the old tests: with the `--copies` call's budget at -1, `trailmark.js:711`, 2 of 78 failed, both by accident). `--copies` has its own call to `otherCopies`, which only one test per copy needed to finish. Fix: "session start: warns of an old cached copy ..." (`copies.test.js`, both copies) also checks that `listInTime` lists the planted copy. Proof: the new test fails in both copies at its new check (`copies.test.js:118`, "the check stopped early: it took too long") with that budget at -1; 2/2 pass as shipped.
- F4 (CONFIRMED in the code). In "0.3.3 hardening: the PreCompact status runs no fsmonitor, hook or submodule ..." (`commits.test.js`, both copies), the git-timeout skip came before the checks that git started nothing (no marks, no `run_command`), so a late run checked neither. They now run first; only the check that status ran waits for an in-time run. Not proven by a forced fault: making git both start a program and run out of time in one run wasn't built (the order is plain in the diff).

Checks after the fix: 62/66 pass, the 4 skips the Windows-only folder names (`--only` over every changed test, both copies); all PASS, handoff-checks 158/246 with 88 skipped, the same as 5566010 (`--sums --quick`).

### Review round 2 (`git diff 91415bb..d6a01ac`, 2026-11-07)

Opus, regression and design. Three findings; each checked here before the fix, fixed in one push:

- A (INFERRED from timings CONFIRMED by the reviewer, not re-run here). F1's lock-free control was the subagent hook even when the commit hook was the one stopped. The reviewer's times, lock busy / commit hook free / subagent hook free: idle 2.9 / 0.87 / 0.35 s; 16 busy loops 5.8 to 6.2 / 3.5 to 4.0 / 1.5 s; 24 busy loops 14.5 to 15.9 / 11 to 12.5 / 3.1 to 3.9 s. So three commit-hook stops under 24 to 30 loops would fail on load alone, which the reviewer didn't reach in 3 runs. Fix: `hookInTime` takes the lock's path, removes it, and runs the stopped hook itself. Proof: the new test fails in both copies, the free run taking 663 and 671 ms with the 20 s wait (the tests from d6a01ac: fail too, with the subagent hook's 367 and 349 ms: on an idle machine the two controls agree, and the difference is only under load).
- B (CONFIRMED by the reviewer, not re-run under load here: at 30 busy loops 1 of 2 runs of unedited d6a01ac failed in both copies; older than this branch). In the busy-lock test the launcher's commit lookup can run out of its own budget (5 s less what the launcher used, `trailmark.js:341`). The notes then get `COMMIT_UNRESOLVED why=git-timeout` in place of the COMMIT line the test expects. It wasn't on "Load-sensitive tests". Fix: the commit hook is repeated while that marker is new and the COMMIT line is missing, three times, then the test skips naming the marker. Proof, with `commitFacts`'s budget at 5 ms in a scratch tree: on the first call per repo, the tests from d6a01ac fail in both copies at the COMMIT line, with `COMMIT_UNRESOLVED why=git-timeout` in the kept notes, the new ones pass 2/2 after a repeat; on every call, the new ones skip 2 of 2, naming the marker; with no forced fault, 2/2 pass. A commit lookup that always runs out still fails `commits.test.js` (12 of 26 per copy, "Proof" above).
- C (CONFIRMED by a simulation, `probe-c.js`; the real rates HYPOTHESIZED). Both copy walks have the same 300 ms budget, so a session start cut short while `--show-names` finished can be time alone, and F2's five tries then failed the test: 2.4% of calls with both late 90% of the time, 90% with session start late 99% and `--show-names` 50%. Fix: once any `--show-names` in the window gives the time reason, the case counts as time (repeat, then skip); ten such tries with none are returned and fail. Simulated, 20,000 calls each: 0%, 0% and 0.09% fail at those rates; the F2 fault (session start always cut short for its own reason) still fails, after 10 tries.
- Also: the PreCompact hardening test reads its trace only if git wrote one (HYPOTHESIZED by the reviewer: a run where no git call started would throw ENOENT before the skip). F3 and F4 had nothing CONFIRMED.

Checks after the fix: 62/66 pass, the 4 skips the Windows-only folder names (`--only` over every changed test, both copies); all PASS, handoff-checks 158/246 with 88 skipped, the same as 5566010 (`--sums --quick`).

### Review round 3 (`git diff d6a01ac..5e90286`, 2026-11-07)

Opus, regression and design. Nothing CONFIRMED wrong in the code; A, B and C each behave as designed (CONFIRMED by round 3's repros, not re-run here):

- A: with the commit hook made 7.5 s slower on its own, 5e90286 skips 2 of 2 and d6a01ac fails 2 of 2 (its control was the cheaper subagent hook). With the lock's wait at 20 s, both fail 2 of 2.
- B: a commit dropped with no marker fails 2 of 2; the commit lookup at 5 ms on every call skips 2 of 2 naming the marker (d6a01ac fails 2 of 2). The payload has no `tool_use_id`, so the hook's same-command rule doesn't apply, and `knownCommits` keeps a repeat from writing a second COMMIT line.
- C: session start's check throwing fails 2 of 2; its budget at -1 on an idle machine fails 2 of 2. With `--show-names` also cut short 30% of the time, 5e90286 skips 2 of 2: the designed cost, since one time reason from `--show-names` lets a fault of session start's own skip under load.

## Faster local checks (2026-11-06, branch `claude/faster-checks` off cf06986)

The two speedups the user agreed to on 2026-11-06 for one small PR after 0.6.0: the suites at the same time in `release-check.sh`, and `trailmark.test.js` split into files. Pushed 2026-11-07 on the user's "Push and open PR", with main's 0.6.0 publish record (5a8dd2a) merged in.

- 01ef1a4: `release-check.sh` starts the three suites in the background, each with its own temp folder (`$T/s1`, `s2`, `s3`: short, since a test's paths repeat it), so a failed test's kept folders still go to its own suite's kept output. One summary line per suite as before, now with the suite's time. Ctrl-C stops the background suites.
- f05b383: each `plugins/*/tests/trailmark.test.js` is now nine files, one or more of its old sections each (`basics`, `sessions`, `hardening`, `commits`, `sweep`, `copies`, `security`, `commit-folders`, and `context-watch` for Claude Code or `codex` for Codex), plus `helpers.js` with what more than one file uses. The code was moved by a script that only cuts at top-level statements and checks the pieces rebuild the old file; a line-by-line comparison finds two changed lines per copy (the sweep test reads `sweepRepeats()`, since `helpers.js` keeps the count) and the new file heads. A file that counts tool-use IDs keeps its own `toolSeq`; the ID prefixes differ, so IDs stay apart. CI and `release-check.sh` take every `*.test.js` of a copy except handoff-checks, so a new file can't be left out. No split file is identical in both copies, so the shared-file list in CI is unchanged.
- 4c79b13: two files at a time in each trailmark suite (`--test-concurrency=2`, `AT_ONCE` in `release-check.sh`), chosen from the runs below.

Measured on this machine (16 logical cores), full `dev/release-check.sh` with `TMPDIR=/e/DevTemp` (the user variable is `E:\DevTemp`; this shell still had the old one, so each run set it), CPU sampled every 5 s. ### Review round 1 (`git diff 5a8dd2a..86fd88a`, 2026-11-07)

Opus for regression, Sonnet for docs, and the Codex review bot on GitHub. No security row: the diff touches none of its files.

- (Codex P2 and Opus, CONFIRMED here.) The Ctrl-C trap's `kill 0` reached whatever started `release-check.sh`: a script started without job control shares its caller's process group. Repro: a wrapper that starts `release-check.sh --only 'past six, a folder a sweep has read'` in the background and sends TERM to it alone; the wrapper died (exit 143). Fixed: each suite starts under `set -m`, so it has a process group of its own, and the trap sends TERM to those groups only, waits for them, then exits 130. With the fix the wrapper survived in every run, the suite's whole process tree (node, its test-file children, git, conhost; 5 to 8 processes, listed by parent id) was gone right after, and Ctrl-C (INT through `timeout -s INT`) did the same. CI never runs this script.
- (Found while checking that fix, CONFIRMED here.) After a stop, the EXIT trap's single `rm -rf` left the stopped suite's folder (`s1/tmp/jbmem-*`) behind in 4 of 5 runs of the fixed trap on Windows, though no process of the suite was left. Windows frees a stopped process's files a moment late (INFERRED). Fixed: the cleanup retries for up to 5 s and says so if it can't. 3 of 3 TERM runs and 1 INT run then left nothing.
- (Sonnet, CONFIRMED.) CONTRIBUTING.md still named `tests/trailmark.test.js`, and so did the head comment of both `handoff-checks.test.js` copies. The Claude Code `commit-folders.test.js` holds seven context-watch tests that its description didn't mention. One CONTRIBUTING command was unquoted (`tests/*.test.js`). All fixed; no doc outside `dev/` names `trailmark.test.js` now.
- (Opus, INFERRED; deferred, see "Deferred to the next version".) `--only` runs every file at Node's default concurrency, not `AT_ONCE`.
- Checked and fine (Opus, CONFIRMED by its scripts, not re-run): every old test is in exactly one new file with an identical body (175/175, 168/168), apart from the two `sweepRepeats()` lines. No file uses a name it neither declares nor imports, and the `toolSeq` prefixes don't collide. The CI line works in bash on all three runners.

### Review round 2 (`git diff 86fd88a..ff2e3e0`, 2026-11-07)

Run by the review-strategy session: Opus found four items in `dev/release-check.sh` and Sonnet nothing in the docs. CI passed 9 of 9 on ff2e3e0. The user: "Fix all four". Fixed in 68f5a6b. The repros are scratch scripts, not in the repo: `round2-repro.sh` runs the same cases on two commits, each in a scratch worktree with a 20 s heartbeat test and a fake `node` added there only, and `f4-stress.sh` races TERM against starting jobs. Each ran on Windows (Git Bash, bash 5.3) and on Linux (WSL Ubuntu, bash 5.2, Node 18, from a local clone). CI on 5a1e1a4 (run 42399384038): 8 of 9 jobs passed; windows-latest Node 26 failed one handoff-checks test, the copy check's budget at session start (under "Load-sensitive tests", not from this PR).

- F1 (CONFIRMED). The trap took INT and TERM but not HUP, and since round 1 the suites have process groups of their own, so a hangup to the script's group (a closed terminal, a dropped SSH) left them running. Repro: start the script as its own job and send HUP to its group. On ff2e3e0: exit 129, the test kept running, on Windows and on Linux. On 68f5a6b: exit 129, the test stopped, on both. Each signal now exits 128 + its number: 130 for INT, 143 for TERM (130 before), 129 for HUP, the shell's own convention, so a caller can tell which one stopped the run.
- F2 (CONFIRMED; trigger HYPOTHESIZED). The stop's `wait` had no bound, and each further signal ran the stop again. Repro: a fake `node` that ignores TERM, INT and HUP, then TERM, TERM and HUP one second apart. On ff2e3e0 the script exited 130 after 2 s and left that suite running, on both systems. That is a different form from Opus's repro, which hung 21 s: either way the stop didn't end the suite. On 68f5a6b it exited 143 after 12 s on Windows and 10 s on Linux, with nothing left: the stop sends TERM, polls the groups for up to 10 s, kills what is left, and ignores further signals meanwhile. A suite that does stop on TERM ends the poll at once (one round; 325 ms on Windows, 205 ms on Linux, `poll-time.sh`), so the bound costs nothing in a normal stop. Native node on Windows ends at TERM, so only an msys child that ignores it can trip the bound there.
- F3 (INFERRED, not tested: no bash before 4.4 here; WSL has 5.2). Under `set -u`, `"${a[@]}"` of an empty array fails as unbound on bash before 4.4, macOS's 3.2 included. `SUITE_PIDS` is gone (see F4), and the expansions that can be empty (`SUITES`, `RESULTS`, `TCC`, `TCX`) use `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}`. `HC` is a fixed list of two and `old` in `keep_dir` is read by index, so neither changed. On bash 5.3 the form gives nothing for an empty array and keeps an element with a space whole (checked).
- F4 (CONFIRMED on Windows, not reproduced on Linux). A signal between a suite's start and the next line, which recorded `$!`, missed that suite. Repro (`f4-stress.sh`, 30 runs each): TERM at a random moment while jobs start. Recording `$!` (as ff2e3e0) left a job running in 30 of 30 runs on Windows and 0 of 30 on Linux. Reading `jobs -rp` (as 68f5a6b) left none in 30 of 30 on both. Chosen: read the groups from the job table, because bash enters a job there as part of starting it, before any trap can run, and `-r` leaves out finished suites, so a stop after `finish_suites` signals no group whose number may have been reused. The table is read through a file. Round 3 found `$(jobs -rp)` gives the same numbers on bash 5.3 and 5.2; the file form stays, since it needs no subshell.
- Neighbors, the same on both systems: TERM from a wrapper that shares the script's group (the wrapper lived, the test stopped), Ctrl-C (INT through `timeout`: exit 130, stopped), a stop before any suite (TERM 1 s into `--quick`: exit 143 at once, no suite started), and a normal `--only` run (the same summary on both commits). No case left a temp folder. Not tested: macOS and bash 3.2.

### A: the context watch (2026-11-04/05)

- New: `hook-context-watch.js` (sandboxed), `lib/contextwatch.js` (launcher side), the `context-watch` entry in `HOOKS` and `hooks.json` (PostToolUse with no matcher, UserPromptSubmit, 10 s), `contextWatch` in `.jbmem.json` (`on`, `steps` 80..99, `reserve` 20000..50000; defaults 85/90/95 and 33000).
- Docs facts (Claude Code docs, read 2026-11-04 by a subagent, quoted with URLs; model-config, env-vars, settings-reference, hooks): `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` wins over the settings (documented, so the HYPOTHESIZED order is now CONFIRMED by the docs); a model's `modelSettings` entry wins over the top-level value in the same file; "auto" is the model's own window; default is the model's context limit (1M for Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+; 200k for others and unknown IDs); the window is capped at the model's context; `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` is a percentage 1..100 of the window and can only lower the point. The 33k reserve is not documented (still INFERRED from `preTokens`).
- Choices: no "fallback window" setting, since the docs give the default per model (the prototype's 200k guess is replaced by it); the window is capped at the model's own; the percentage override is honored. A request ignores `hints.minMinutesBetween` (last chance before the compaction) and sets `lastHintAt`, so a milestone hint does not follow straight away.
- Speed: the launcher runs `contextwatch.fastPath()` before loading anything else and exits below the earliest step any configuration allows (80% of the window less 50k). Measured (`cwtime.js`, scratch, 15 runs each, 1.2 MB transcript tail): bare `node -e 0` median 70 ms; the hook below the step median 89 ms (min 82, max 122). Before moving the fast path ahead of the module loads it was 292 ms against 172 ms bare (a busier moment), about 50 ms of it module loading. A test checks that no child process starts below the step.
- Start over: the launcher reads the transcript back to the time of the last request and passes the smallest size and any `compact_boundary` since; the hook starts over on a compaction, a shrink by a fifth, a fall below 75% of the compaction point, or when it could not read back that far. Nothing is written below the first step.
- Codex: not ported. Codex rollouts do record usage (`token_count` events with `last_token_usage` and `model_context_window`, CONFIRMED in a local rollout file) but its compaction point (`model_auto_compact_token_limit`, unset here) and default are not established, and its hooks have no UserPromptSubmit. Claude Code only in 0.6.0; README and CHANGELOG to say so. trailmark-watchdog does none of this (it watches plugin files).
- Tests (`trailmark.test.js`, 9): the prototype's 14 cases plus the steps-before-the-point check at 400k and 200k, the worktree/sandbox case, refused transcript paths, the variable, the percentage override, the cap, prompts, a shrink and a dip. All 9 fail on d6b705e and pass now.

- Regression and security (Opus): nothing CONFIRMED in the changed code. `fastPath` is the only caller of `readUsage` without `since` (CONFIRMED by grep). Crafted transcripts through the old and new `readUsage` (CONFIRMED with a scratch script): the new one returns null for a boundary followed by a `<synthetic>` entry, by a sidechain request, by 1.4 MB or 8.6 MB of tool results, for two compactions in a row and for compaction, request, compaction; a sidechain boundary still gives 315000. Tool output, prompts and file text can't make a main-thread boundary (they are escaped strings or nested values); forging one takes a direct append to the transcript, and silences the watch only until the next request. The extra check costs 2 ms or less against about 70 ms of Node start.
  - An automatic compaction mid-turn can put a tool result between the boundary and the next request: one of 76 boundaries in local transcripts has the in-flight `tool_use` copied with zero usage, then its `tool_result`, then the request (INFERRED that the hook sees this order; that transcript's timestamps are out of order). The old code used the 966k size from before that compaction; the new one stays silent. The docs now name both cases.
  - The test's last assertion ("the steps started over") would also pass through the shrink rule, so it doesn't prove the boundary path on its own; the fix doesn't claim that path.
- Docs (Sonnet): no contradictions between docs and code; MANUAL.md and CHANGELOG.md need nothing. Fixed after it: "the next prompt comes before the next request" was stated as fact (now "can come", with the mid-turn case), "a compaction" now says the main thread's, two counts and two run descriptions now say whose they are, the probes moved from the session scratchpad to `dev/probes/` so they can be re-run, the 42-test claim has its labels, the test counts say what they count, and a three-item list was reworded. The commit message of 887e17f keeps the older wording.

Cause, CONFIRMED here with a junction (this account can't make symlinks): on Windows an exclusive create (`'wx'`) goes through a link or junction at the name whose target is missing, and makes the target. It is used for the lock, `.break` and the state file's `.bad` copy. CHANGELOG: "Memory folder (Windows)". New test: "lock and state copy: a link whose target is missing is never made through (0.6.0)" (handoff-checks, both copies; it runs everywhere, with a junction on Windows).

### PR #5: CLAUDE.md and `release-check.sh` (merged 2026-11-05, d230681)

- From the 0.6.0 work, landed apart from the release. Besides what its brief asked for (a failing suite's kept output, `--only`, the load-sensitive list below, the CLAUDE.md rules), `release-check.sh` gained seven things:
  1. A name pattern that matches no test fails with "no test ran". Node counts each file with no matching test as one passing test.
  2. `--only` keeps its output even when it passes, so a skip's reason stays.
  3. Only the 20 newest kept run folders stay.
  4. `--only` refuses `--sums` and `--zip`.
  5. `--help` prints the whole header; it printed fixed lines 2 to 12.
  6. Paths print in `C:/...` form on Windows.
  7. The summary heading names `--only` and says whether the tree had uncommitted changes.

### `TAG_LIKE`'s time (2026-11-06, the user: "Pull into 0.6.0")

- Found while fixing round 9's F1 and listed under "Deferred to the next version" in 71d7a78; moved here. In `store.js` since 75c9957 (0.5.0) or earlier. v0.5.1 has it (CONFIRMED with v0.5.1's `store.js`: 324 ms at n = 600, 2,536 ms at n = 1,200).
- The cause (CONFIRMED by the pattern and the timings): in 71d7a78's `TAG_LIKE`, runs in a row could each take invisible characters, from an opening tag's name to the spaces before its end. With no tag end after the run, the engine tried every way to split it, so the time grew with the run's length cubed: `escapeTags('<a' + U+200B x 3,000 + '!')` took about 43 s on 71d7a78.
- At session start (CONFIRMED by the session-start test below, on 71d7a78's `store.js`): with such a line in the handoff, the launcher stopped the hook after about 9.1 s ("hook-session-start.js took too long and was stopped"), so the session got no handoff.
- The user, through the review-strategy session: "Pull into 0.6.0". It is the one item pulled through the scope freeze.
- Fix, both copies' `store.js`: `TAG_LIKE` is built from strings so that each run matches a stretch of text one way only. The comment above it gives the reasons:
  - The run before a name's separator takes no separator, and the run after it stops at the first character that can't be in a name.
  - U+FEFF is both invisible and a space, so those runs leave it to the tag's end.
  - Four Hangul fillers are both letters and invisible: the run before an opening tag's name stops at them, and the name starts there.
  - A role word's letters are taken whole, with a lookahead and `\1`.
  - Every class that holds the invisible characters writes them as `TAG_INV`, so `SHOWN_TAG_LIKE`'s builder still finds all 10. `TAG_LIKE` and `SHOWN_TAG_LIKE` are exported for the tests.
  - Bounding each run (64 characters, the deferred entry's first idea) wasn't taken: a tag after a longer run would go unescaped, where 71d7a78 escaped it.
- Fail-closed (CONFIRMED, scratch scripts `tag2-diff.js` and `scan2.js`): over 775,958 strings, every string of up to 4 symbols over a 26-symbol alphabet after `<` and 300,000 seeded random ones, the new pattern and 71d7a78's escape the same text, plain and shown, with 0 differences either way. A scan of U+0000 to U+2FFFF at five places in a tag, 983,040 inputs per copy, against 71d7a78's `store.js`: 0 escapes missed and 0 added, on the plain path and on the shown path. F1's count (escaped on the plain path, not on the shown one) is 0 for both over those five places. Over every string of up to 4 symbols it is 37,066 of 475,255, the same on old and new (CONFIRMED by Fable in the combined round, and here on main with `dev/probes/tag-shown-gaps.js`; the deferred list).
- Time (scratch `tag2-diff.js`): at n = 3,000 the ten shapes the time test uses take at most 0.3 ms each, plain and shown.

In all 9 `sample` shows the parent in `SyncProcessRunner::TryInitializeAndRunLoop` waiting in `kevent`, and `lsof` shows it still holding the other end of the child's stdin socket. In 8 the child is blocked in `read` on fd 0 inside `readFileSync` (`hookio.readPayload` for the hook); in the ninth it had exited by the time it was sampled. The launcher hands it over as JSON in `JBMEM_PAYLOAD`, as `JBMEM_GIT` already travels, and nothing on stdin, so no socket is written to at all. A field filter alone would have left a long command on stdin. `JBMEM_PAYLOAD` is scrubbed from the launcher's environment with the other `JBMEM_` variables, and `readPayload` takes it only when `JBMEM_LAUNCHED` is 1. Windows caps a variable at 32,767 characters, so a payload over 30,000 characters of JSON starts no hook script, and the launcher says so on stderr. In practice that takes a very long command. ### Confirmed since review

- CONFIRMED (2026-11-02, git 2.56.0.windows.2): Git for Windows takes `..` as text from a `.git` that is a junction. With `top\.git` a junction to `elsewhere\gitdir`, both `include.path = ../x` and a `commondir` of `../common` were read from `top\`, not `elsewhere\`. That held when git found `.git` itself (it reported the origin as `.git/../x`) and when it was given `--git-dir`. A copy without a junction read the same files, which shows the probe worked. The check would start where the junction leads, so the two would read different files, and the `linked-gitdir` refusal on Windows (`gitbin.js`) is needed. Not tested: other pointers (`objects/info/alternates`, a worktree's `gitdir` file) and directory symlinks as opposed to junctions.

### Done: the silent sweep skip (2026-11-03, branch `claude/loving-cannon-9abde1`)

- A sweep that runs out of time sets `stopped: 'out-of-time'` (`trailmark.js` `sweepFacts` at each budget gate; `gitfacts.js` `sweepCommits` when a folder is left unread because of the 800 ms gate or a git call refused or timed out). `write-handoff` prints "commit sweep skipped: out of time ..." and session start adds it to the warnings. Only fixed text is printed. `swept` moves only for folders read, as before. Timer values unchanged. `JBMEM_TEST_SWEEP_MS` can only lower the sweep's budget.
- Tests (each copy): the 0.3.4 sweep test repeats a sweep that reports the skip, for up to 90 s, and counts what all of them logged. If every sweep in that window runs out of time it is skipped with the reason, since nothing a finished sweep logs can be checked then. ### Done: repoRoot when git times out (2026-11-03)

- The defect: when `git rev-parse` timed out (3 s, or 1000 ms for commit-start, up to 500 ms in the sweep), `lib/paths.js` `repoRoot` returned the folder itself. In a linked worktree or a subfolder, `findMemoryDir` then looked for a memory folder of that folder's own.
- What it did, CONFIRMED on 4182717 with a stub that makes `git rev-parse` throw ETIMEDOUT (`node -r`, launcher process only), both copies:
  - commit-start in a linked worktree wrote no record and printed nothing (with git normal it writes one). This caused the burst failure of "a commit command still running" above.
  - The worse case, HYPOTHESIZED before, is CONFIRMED: `dir --json` in a worktree resolved to the worktree's own project folder (Claude Code makes one for each folder a session runs in) with method `key:...`, which needs no `--force`, and `init` set that folder up (Claude Code copy; the Codex copy's `init` needs `JBMEM_CODEX_INIT=1` and resolved the same folder).
- The fix: both timeout branches of `repoRoot` (after `--git-common-dir` and after `--show-toplevel`) return `localRepoRoot(cwd)`, the lookup from `.git` entries on disk that the kept-out path already uses, else the folder itself. Errors other than a timeout are handled as before. With the same stub, `dir` and `init` in a worktree now use the main checkout's folder and commit-start writes its record.
- Test (each copy): "0.5.1 paths: when git times out in a linked worktree or a subfolder..." runs the launcher with that stub: `dir` from a worktree and a subfolder, `init` from a worktree, and the commit-start record. Fails on 4182717 at `dir` (the worktree's folder) in both copies; passes now. The stub fails every `rev-parse`, so only the first timeout branch runs; the second (after `--show-toplevel`) is reached only with git older than 2.31 and is untested.
- Reviews: Opus on the test commit d01ccd4 found nothing (it checked by mutation that the wrapped tests still fail on a real bug). Fable on the repoRoot change: safe to ship. `localRepoRoot` gives the root git would give for a main checkout, linked worktree, subfolder and bare-repo worktree; a `.git` file planted to point straight at another repo's `.git` gives the planted folder (git gives the other repo), as on the kept-out path; the memory folder stays under the projects folder whatever root is chosen. One CONFIRMED finding, reproduced here: after the timeout, `localRepoRoot` can run `git config --file` once more (3000 ms limit) when `.git/config` holds `//` (an https remote). The comment that said "no second call" is corrected; the time budget is deferred below.

  - Proven (2026-11-03, the user asked for it): with every core busy (`burn.js`, 32 threads), the test failed 3 of 3 (`expected: 'submodule-pointer'`, `actual: 'git-timeout'`, 7.7 to 8.7 s each). CONFIRMED two ways to run out: (a) `farModules` started with 2991 and 4338 ms left and checked 49 and 148 of the 168 module gitdirs that come before `s7` in listing order (about 45 and 24 ms each) before its gate (`left() < 800`) stopped it; (b) the first git call (`branch`) took 4149 ms and timed out, so the walk never ran. Idle, the walk checks all 168 in 2.2 to 3.4 s (13 to 20 ms each) and the test passes. The walk starts no git: one `farModules` over 200 gitdirs made 26,403 `lstat` calls on 1,810 distinct paths (`localPath` lstat's every part of every path, about 132 calls per gitdir). Status is skipped either way (fail closed); the test's reason and its `farGitConfig < 2000 ms` check (2099 ms in one loaded run) depend on time. Decided (the user): "Speed up the walk".
- Fix (gitbin.js, both copies): `localPath` keeps each lstat result in `LSTAT_SEEN` while one check runs (the outermost `withShare` call) and drops it when that check returns. `localPath` outside a check uses no cache.
- Measured (`measure.sh`, scratch; 3 runs each, 200 module gitdirs): the walk alone, idle 2.1 to 2.4 s before and 0.37 to 0.38 s after; with every core busy 16.9 to 27.1 s before and 2.4 to 3.0 s after; 26,403 lstat calls before, 2,412 after. `gitFacts` with the hook's 5 s budget, idle: 2.4 to 2.9 s before, 0.8 to 0.9 s after. With every core busy it still runs out (`git-timeout`) before and after, since git's own calls take seconds then; the walk was no longer the cause in the run that reached it (28 gitdirs in 442 ms, started with 1241 ms left).

"... what one check found is not kept for the next" swaps a folder for a junction between two checks; it passes on e01c60f (no cache) and fails on a version whose cache isn't dropped. The superprojects test gives `gitFacts` 60 s (its subject is which gitdir is found, not the hook's time). Under full load the three passed 3 of 3 (before: the old test failed 3 of 3).
- Review: Fable on the gitbin.js diff found nothing CONFIRMED wrong. CONFIRMED by it: no cache outlives a check, a throw inside one included; no wrapped check calls another; `localPath` outside a check (plainfile.js, health.js, gitfacts.js and others) stays uncached. Notes, not changed: `farLfsFile` and `farLfsEntries` don't use `withShare`, so they run uncached (the slower, safe side); the older per-folder `farCache` of `farGitConfig` verdicts is kept across checks, as before 0.5.1; a swap during a check gives the same verdict as a fresh check unless its target is a share, which an attacker could equally set up after the check.

## Decided not to fix (2026-11-03, the user: "Leave both")

- A worktree `gitdir` file with trailing spaces keeps git out with the reason `network-gitdir`, which misleads. The note that git trims them is RULED OUT (2026-11-03): git 2.56.0.windows.2 and git 2.43 (Linux) both refuse such a worktree ("not a git repository" / "gitfile does not point to a valid repository"), so keeping git out matches git; only the reason word is wrong. Reason: git itself refuses such a worktree, so keeping git out is right; only the reason word misleads.
- A pending commit-start record written by trailmark-codex 0.4.5 has no `host` field and can be released early, within 11 minutes of upgrading. CONFIRMED (2026-11-03, `openCommitStart` on a record without `host`, a later command of the same session done): released, where a record with `host: codex` holds; both are released once 11 minutes pass. The field came in 2484cbd (in v0.5.0). Codex users coming from 0.5.0 already have `host` (0.5.0 is published, 2026-11-02), so the window applies to upgrades from 0.4.5, and it needs a Codex commit command running across the upgrade and the same session finishing a later one inside 11 minutes, and the effect is one commit logged by the wrong session's sweep. Reason: it needs a Codex commit running across the upgrade and a later command of the same session within 11 minutes; the worst effect is one commit logged under the wrong session, and it expires on its own.

A folder added to `commitDirs` is swept from the session's start, so commits another session made there since then are logged "(found later)" under this one; true of any `commitDirs` entry, the background case only adds a way in.

Outside Windows, after `git rm` of a submodule, `.git/modules/<name>` stays with `core.worktree = ../../../<name>`, a folder that is gone; `localPath` refuses the `..` after it, so `farModules` gives `network-config` and `git status` is skipped (`submodule-pointer`) in that superproject until the leftover is removed. CONFIRMED in WSL with git 2.43 (a superproject with two submodules, one removed); Windows gives `''`. Fails closed.
- (Same.) A relative setting in a gitdir is also read from `CHECK_CWD`, the folder of the last `farGitConfig` call in the process, so a direct `farModules` call can give a different answer after a check of another folder. CONFIRMED on Windows: `''`, then `network-config` after a check of `//evil.invalid/share/x`, then `''` after a check of the folder itself. `gitFacts` always checks its folder first. It can only add refusals.
- (Same.) "git checks: on Windows a .git that is a junction keeps git out" failed in local runs of handoff-checks (`EBUSY` making the junction at `r\.git`, or `EPERM` moving `.git`): 2 of 6 runs of the file as committed at 7eeb33c, 1 of 6 with PR #1's fixture change, and once in a full release check, so not from that change. On this machine, moving a just-written folder or making a junction in its place fails now and then even when no process was started: 150 runs gave 11 rename EPERM and 1 junction EBUSY with plain files, 15 and 5 with a git repo (`juncloop.js`, scratch). Something holds new files for a moment; Defender's real-time protection is on, so INFERRED, not proven, which process. Not changed in 0.5.1. Again on 2026-11-04: failed once in the full release check after the leftover `onlyFiles` fix (that code isn't reached for a junction `.git`, which `farGit` refuses first on Windows), then passed 6 of 6 alone and in a full run of both handoff-checks copies; the error text wasn't kept by the check.

- (Fable review of 4152c3c; older than it.) On a file system that doesn't report entry types (d_type unknown), Node's `readdirSync` lstat's each decoded name, which fails for a name that isn't valid UTF-8, so the listing throws and `linkedEntries` passes over that whole folder unwalked. CONFIRMED from Node 18 and 26 source; HYPOTHESIZED on a real file system (ext4 and tmpfs report d_type).

- (Found in the Fable review of e6c24fa, CONFIRMED by it with the stub.) When another command holds the state file's lock for more than 2 s, the commit hook's fallback writes `COMMIT_UNRESOLVED why=git-timeout` but neither tells Claude nor records the folder in `commitDirs`, so a commit in another folder is still not swept. Not a regression (the same as before 0.5.1); the docs name the exception. A fix could print the note without the sweep promise in that path.

- Found while fixing the sweep (2026-11-03):
  - Four other sweep tests failed with every core busy. Proven (2026-11-03): each was run alone, 2 rounds per suite, from a copy of the test file that logs every launcher call and `sweepCommits` result (scratch only, not committed):
    - "a commit made after the sweep started": 4 of 4 failed. `sweepCommits` returned `stopped: out-of-time`, read 0 of 1 folders, in 2.9 to 3.3 s. CONFIRMED out-of-time skip.
    - "the sweeping session's own open records": 4 of 4 failed. write-handoff took 8.8 to 14 s and printed the skip; no COMMIT lines; `swept` empty. CONFIRMED out-of-time skip.
    - "a commit command still running": 4 of 4 failed the same way. CONFIRMED out-of-time skip.
    - "another clone with its own memory folder": 1 of 4 failed on the skip. 3 of 4 failed earlier, where B's commit hook ran 9.8 to 11.8 s, its git calls ran out of its 5 s budget, and it logged `COMMIT_UNRESOLVED why=git-timeout` instead of the commit. A different cause (the commit hook's own budget). Fixed in 0.5.1, see "the commit hook when git times out" above.
    - The first three now use `settle` / `sweepTest` (`settleCall` for the direct `sweepCommits` calls). Rerun with each test alone, 2 rounds per suite: full load, 10 skipped with the reason and 2 passed; 20 s bursts, 15 of 16 passed; idle, 16 of 16 passed.
    - The one burst failure ("a commit command still running", Codex copy): B's commit-start record was never written (no `pending/` folder), so A's sweep took B's commit. The hook resolves the memory folder with a 1000 ms git timeout; it timed out, `repoRoot` fell back to the worktree, and the hook found nothing set up and exited silently. CONFIRMED with a stub that times out `git rev-parse` (`node -r`): on 4182717, both copies, commit-start in a linked worktree writes its record when git is normal and none when git times out. This is the `repoRoot` item below.
  - After a `git rev-parse` timeout, `repoRoot` calls `localRepoRoot`, which can read `.git/config` with `git config --file` (gitbin.js `configEntries`, fixed 3000 ms limit) when the file holds `//`. CONFIRMED (stub, worktree with an https remote): one extra call, about 70 ms when git is fast. When git is slow enough to time out, this can add up to 3 s per config file, past the caller's budget (1000 ms for commit-start, up to 500 ms in the sweep). A hook that runs over is stopped and says so. Fix: pass the caller's time limit through `localRepoRoot` to `configEntries` (gitbin.js, a security file: Fable review).
  - (Fixed in 0.5.1, see "repoRoot when git times out" above.) `lib/paths.js` `repoRoot` fell back to the folder itself when git timed out.
- (Fixed in 0.5.1, see above.) The `0.3.4 sweep` test fails when git is slow, because a sweep that runs out of time is skipped without a trace. CONFIRMED (2026-11-02):
  - The one failure (zip build, 16:36) left its sandbox in `%TEMP%\jbmem-4hucLT`: `swept` never moved past the first write (21:36:41), and the resume hook took 7.8 s (p50 3.7 s over 62 runs) and logged nothing.
  - Defender's log shows another workload (a starflight test audit: python, node, pwsh) writing files from 16:36:42.4 to at least 16:36:58, which covers both sweeps that recorded nothing and none of those that worked.
  - Reproduced: with every core busy (`burn.js`, 32 threads), 3 of 3 runs failed and the 5 runs after the load passed. Under load each git call took 0.6 to 1.3 s (normally about 0.1 s), and the write-handoff sweep never reached `git log -g`: the budget gates (`trailmark.js` `sweepFacts`: 1300, 1000 ms; `gitfacts.js` `sweepCommits`: 800 ms) stopped it first.
  - The product is safe: `swept` doesn't advance, so the next sweep finds those commits. The defects are that the skip is silent and the test asserts an outcome that depends on time. Fix for 0.5.1: report a skipped sweep (for example "commit sweep skipped: out of time"), and have the test accept that report plus a later sweep that logs the commits, instead of requiring this sweep to finish.
- `tools/windows` scripts and installers: no review findings open.

## Load-sensitive tests (listed 2026-11-05)

These tests fail, or skip themselves, on a busy machine and pass on an idle one. Since `claude/faster-checks` (f05b383) the old `trailmark.test.js` numbers below point into split files: the busy lock is in `sessions.test.js`, the sweep tests in `sweep.test.js`, `security.test.js` and `commit-folders.test.js` (#150 in `security.test.js`), and the git-facts tests in `basics.test.js` (16), `commits.test.js` (89) and `sweep.test.js` (108). The local check runs two files at a time per suite because of the commit-list and sweep entries ("Faster local checks", above). Most of the proof comes from the 0.6.0 work (`claude/release-0.6.0`, its "Deferred to the next version"), where the fixes are deferred. A failure of one of them is put down to load only when its kept output shows the sign named here; anything else is a new failure. A test joins this list only with a proven cause (CLAUDE.md, "Checking a change"). Busy loops: `node -e "for(;;){}"`, started in the background as many times as the entry says. Since `claude/load-proof-tests` (2026-11-07, "Load-proof tests" above), the busy-lock bound, the commit hook's time limit and the copy check's budget are off this list: their tests repeat the call, or skip with the reason, and their entries as they stood are in that section. The commit-list and git-facts entries are narrower.

- The commit list at session start. Tests: the handoff-checks tests that expect a COMMITS section, in both copies: the "commits since the handoff: ..." tests (test 12 is "... a branch named like the SHA does not stand in for it"), "injection: invisible tag characters and bidi overrides never reach the session-start text (loop round 9)", "cut note: an oversized handoff stays inside injectChars ..." and "fit: a small injectChars holds with a commit list, a snapshot and warnings" (added 2026-11-05: no COMMITS section in both copies, in the full checks of c7a194a at 13:02 and 14:24 while a game ran; test 13 in the Codex copy, CONFIRMED from the kept TAP's location, and 112 in the Claude Code copy, since handoff-checks numbers both copies' files in one run). Sign: no COMMITS section in the session-start text, or "HEAD has 1 newer commit, the newest 0 shown:" over an empty list. CONFIRMED on the 0.6.0 branch with the code as at d6b705e (`loadrepro.js`, scratch: 0 of 5 runs failed idle, 5 of 5 with 16 busy loops), and again on 2026-11-05 at about 72% CPU. Seen again at d6b705e on 2026-11-05 09:39 EST: `--only 'a branch named like the SHA'` failed in both copies with no COMMITS section (10.5 s each), and passed 2 of 2 on the next run. CPU sampled just after the failure was 45 to 54% with 46 node processes, so load as the cause of that run is INFERRED. Repro: 16 busy loops, then `dev/release-check.sh --only 'commits since the handoff'`. The product defect is deferred: the text should say git was too slow to list the commits; a test-only time budget would make the tests hold. Since `claude/load-proof-tests`, each of these tests tries three times, so a failure with this sign now means three in a row.
  - Since batch F (92794c1, "Batch F" above), the sign changed: when git runs out of time the text says "git ran out of time" in place of leaving the section out or "the newest 0 shown". The tests try three times on that sign, then skip with "git ran out of time at 3 session starts in a row (left=... budget=... git=...)" after a control that only load passes (the launcher's `JBMEM_SHOW_SINCE` line must show under 400 ms left before git, or git spending its budget less 300 ms). So load shows here only as skips; a failure of these tests, with or without the old sign, is new and gets investigated.
  - Since RS-T-startstopped (2026-11-16, section "Next version: RS-T-startstopped"), a second sign of load is handled in `handoff-checks.test.js`: the launcher stopping the session-start script at its time limit ("hook-session-start.js took too long and was stopped"). `start()` tries three times on that sign; each stop must match the launcher's rule in its `JBMEM_SHOW_RUN` line, and after the third the script alone with 30 s must answer. Then the tests wrapped in `sinceTest` or `copiesTest` skip with "the launcher stopped the session-start hook at its time limit 3 times in a row (spent=... timeout=...)"; the 13 other tests that call `start()` fail with that text (RS-T-startunwrapped). Since RS-T-startdirect (2026-11-22), two tests that start the hook with their own `spawnSync` take the same tries and skip with the same text (`startTest`): "sweep: huge swept, commitDirsAt and commitDirs in a state file ..." and "session start: an install path usablePath refuses gets a warning ...". The cause is CONFIRMED: reproduced with 16 busy loops and traced with a step probe. Repro: 16 busy loops, then `dev/release-check.sh --only 'commits since the handoff: listed at session start'` (1 of 6 runs on 2a0551c).
- The sweep tests that skip themselves. Tests: those wrapped in `sweepTest` in `trailmark.test.js` (9 per copy at d6b705e: the "0.3.4 sweep: ..." tests, "0.5.1 sweep: ..." and the "0.5.1 commit hook: ..." timeout and background tests). Sign: a skip, not a failure, with "every sweep for 90 s ran out of time" (`SweepsOutOfTime`), so load shows only as a higher skipped count. CONFIRMED in code (`settle`, `settleCall` and `sweepTest` in `trailmark.test.js`) and with every core busy on 2026-11-03 (0.5.1 work: 6 and 7 skips in a row, no sweep finished in 90 s). On the 0.6.0 branch the Codex copy had 17 skipped at 72% CPU against 16 at 23%; that the 17th was a sweep test is INFERRED (that run's output wasn't kept). A skip on an idle machine needs reading: a bug that made every sweep run out of time would also show as skips (Fable, 0.5.1). Repro: one busy loop per core, then `dev/release-check.sh --only '^0\.3\.4 sweep'`; `--only` keeps the TAP output, where the skip reason is. At 7fb6d6e (2026-11-05) there are 12 per copy, and the first to skip is "0.6.0 commit folders: past six, a folder a sweep has read since it joined goes first ..." (seven folders per sweep, the most of any). Its sign: "every sweep for 90 s ran out of time (N in a row)". It skipped in both copies in the full check on 7fb6d6e, one more skip per suite than before PR #4's fixes. Run alone in both copies with versions alternating, while about 53 node processes of other work kept the CPU at 31 to 100%:
  - 93e1231's `store.js` (before `openNew`) skipped 2 of 4 and HEAD's 4 of 4 (B A A B, 12:06 to 12:15).
  - 3f07517's (before both PR #4 fixes) skipped 4 of 4 and HEAD's 2 of 4 (C A A C, 12:17 to 12:25).
  - The code before both fixes skips at least as often, so neither fix is the cause (CONFIRMED). The sweep's budget is in the launcher (`sweepFacts`), which takes no lock; `openNew` adds about 0.3 ms per lock (300 cycles per run, alternating: 1.19 to 1.47 ms against 0.91 to 1.20). Load as the cause is INFERRED: the CPU log doesn't set the passing runs apart from the skipping ones.
  - Repro: `dev/release-check.sh --only 'past six, a folder a sweep has read'` on a busy machine. CI's nine jobs are the idle check (PR #4, in the 0.6.0 section).
  - 2026-11-06 (f05b383): load as the cause is CONFIRMED for the load other test processes make. Run alone, it skipped in both copies while handoff-checks and both trailmark suites ran in the background (CPU 47%, 33 node processes) and passed as that load ended; seven busy loops at the same CPU did not make it skip (2 of 2). Details under "Faster local checks".
- The git-facts budget (added 2026-11-05, with the review-strategy session). Tests (the Codex `trailmark.test.js` numbers at c7a194a; the same tests in the Claude Code copy): 16 "launcher: hooks run sandboxed with launcher-collected git facts", 89 "0.3.3 hardening: the PreCompact status runs no fsmonitor, hook or submodule git" and 108 "0.3.4 commits: another session's commit in the same folder while a command ran is left to that session when git printed this command's". Sign: the git-timeout marker in the failed test's kept folder: `uncommitted=unknown` on the PRE_COMPACT line, "Uncommitted files: not read (git-timeout)" in a snapshot, or `COMMIT_UNRESOLVED why=git-timeout`. The product writes it only when git ran out of its budget, so a failure that shows it is this mechanism, and one without it is new and gets investigated. Seen in the full check of c7a194a's tree (2026-11-05 13:02, a busy machine). Since `claude/load-proof-tests`, the three tests repeat the step, or skip, when the marker shows, so the marker no longer fails them; 108's last step can still fail without it (the side pass, below).
  - Proof (2026-11-05 15:58 to 16:02, a clone of df88236, `dev/repro-git-timeout.sh`): as shipped, all pass. With the launcher's two git budgets cut to 5 ms, all three fail in both copies and leave the marker: 89 at its 13:02 assertion, 16 one assertion earlier (the commit hook runs out too), 108 at its first step. With each git call 500 ms slower, 89 fails at its 13:02 assertion in both copies, and the Codex 16 at its 13:02 assertion with the 13:02 log: branch and head read, `uncommitted=unknown` (CONFIRMED). The Claude Code 16 passed in that run. What made git run out at 13:02 is INFERRED: three suites at once, a game, Unity, Edge and Codex sessions.
  - 108: at 13:02 only its last step failed (line 2772, "via an alias" and "explicit"). A uniform slowdown fails it at its first step (5 ms budgets) or not at all (500, 900 and 1,300 ms more per git call, both copies), so the 13:02 failure point is not reproduced. Measured at idle (16:03, each git call logged in the clone): every step's main pass gets about 4,920 ms and makes 3 or 4 git calls taking about 190 to 280 ms. The last step alone adds a 1,000 ms side pass for another session's folders (`gitfacts.js:547`), whose timeout leaves the commits with this command and can't write the marker. So the steps use about the same of the budget, and why only the last ran out at 13:02 is HYPOTHESIZED: one slow git call, or slow process starts.
- The RS-T-lockagestep tests with an ended holder (added 2026-11-22, PR #113): the six that use `deadLockAt` or `deadLabel`, in both copies ("lock: with the clock moved, a dead holder's lock is broken after 5 s of watching it", "... the watch starts again when the lock changes", "... a .break file is not removed for its age, ...", "lock: a clock step at a .break file's age, or between it and the clock check, ...", "lock: a clock step after the .break file is taken ..." and "lock: a clock moved 1.2 s keeps a dead holder's lock ..."). Sign: a skip, not a failure, with "pid N of an ended holder is in use again, so the test cannot tell". A test skips only where its result is one a live pid could explain (since review round 5): a lock kept where it expects one kept, and a lock not broken where it expects one broken. Cause CONFIRMED by Opus by a run (RS-T-lockagestep review round 4, F3, not re-run): before the skip, the relabel test failed once in about 14 runs with "pid 41888 is in use again", that pid given to a new process within about 6.5 s of its holder's end; that other work's process starts make the reuse this quick is INFERRED. Repro: `dev/release-check.sh --only 'the watch starts again when the lock changes'` on a busy machine.
- Not in this list, since their causes aren't proven to be load (both are in the 0.6.0 deferred list): the `git init -q` failures in the entry "Seen 2026-11-05 while two sessions ran handoff-checks at once" (HYPOTHESIZED: processes failing to start); the same `--quick` check at d6b705e alone on a quiet machine then passed 90 of 176 with 86 skipped and none failed (2026-11-05 10:21 EST, one run). And "Windows, long paths", a matter of path length rather than load: init is refused when the memory folder's path is too long, which a deep temp folder reaches.
